_README_FOR_HUMANS: Nervous about the setup? Copy this ENTIRE file, paste it into any AI chat (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot), and send the message: 'Walk me through setting up Oddjob step by step.' The AI will use the instructions below to guide you start to finish.
_instructions_for_ai: You are an onboarding assistant for a tool called 'Oddjob'. A non-technical user has pasted this file to get help setting it up and using it. Your job: (1) Greet them and ask what operating system they use (Windows, Mac, or Linux) and what they want to do first (try it locally, or set up the automatic cloud schedule). (2) Walk through the steps in 'setup_steps' ONE AT A TIME, in order. After each step, ask them to confirm it worked (use the 'verify' field) before moving on. (3) Explain every step in plain language — assume they have never used a terminal. Give them the exact command to copy, matched to their OS. (4) When they need an API key, use 'api_keys' to tell them exactly where to click. (5) Once set up, use 'commands' and 'presets' to show them how to make their first video. (6) If they hit an error, check 'troubleshooting' first. (7) Never skip steps or assume prior knowledge. Be encouraging and concise.

project.name: Oddjob
project.tagline: Your silent henchman for short-form content — he handles all the odd jobs.
project.what_it_does: An automated bot that creates and posts short vertical videos (YouTube Shorts style). It can (a) find trending news in your chosen topic, write a script, fact-check it, add an AI voiceover + captions + footage, and auto-post it; and (b) 'promo mode' — turn YOUR own song, product, or link into a post. It runs free on a schedule in the cloud via GitHub Actions (no server needed).
project.good_to_know: The only thing that can cost money is the Google Gemini API, and only past its free tier. At the default 3 posts/day it is free or a few cents/month. YouTube posting, the voiceover, and the footage are always free.

setup_steps.title: Install the prerequisites
setup_steps.what: Install Python 3.11+, ffmpeg, and Git from the links in what_you_need.software.
setup_steps.verify: Run 'python --version' and 'ffmpeg -version' in a terminal — both should print a version, not an error.

setup_steps.title: Download Oddjob
setup_steps.verify: You are now inside a folder with a README.md and a 'socialbot' folder.

setup_steps.title: Create a virtual environment and install dependencies

how.mac_linux: python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt

setup_steps.verify: pip install finishes without red errors.

setup_steps.title: Create your settings file
setup_steps.what: Open the new .env file in a text editor — you'll paste keys into it in the next steps.
setup_steps.verify: A file named .env exists in the folder.

setup_steps.title: Add your Gemini key
setup_steps.what: Get a key from Google AI Studio (see api_keys.gemini) and put it in .env after GEMINI_API_KEY=
setup_steps.verify: The .env line reads GEMINI_API_KEY=AQ... (your actual key).

setup_steps.title: (Optional) Add a Pexels key
setup_steps.what: For real stock footage. See api_keys.pexels. Put it after PEXELS_API_KEY=. Skip to use a gradient background instead.

setup_steps.title: Set up YouTube uploading
setup_steps.what: Follow api_keys.youtube exactly — it has its own click-by-click sub-steps. Then run the one-time login.
setup_steps.verify: A browser opens; after you approve, the terminal says the token was saved.

setup_steps.title: Pick your topic and style
setup_steps.what: In .env, set CONTENT_NICHE (what topics to cover) and CONTENT_TONE (the narrator's vibe). See 'presets' for copy-paste examples.

setup_steps.title: Make your first test video (no posting)
setup_steps.what: This finds a topic, writes + fact-checks a script, and renders one video into the review queue WITHOUT posting it.
setup_steps.verify: Terminal prints 'queued for review' with an id.

setup_steps.title: Watch your test video

how.all: python -m socialbot.cli list   (then)   python -m socialbot.cli open <the-id>

setup_steps.verify: The clip plays in your video player.

setup_steps.title: Post it (when you're happy)
setup_steps.what: Keep YOUTUBE_PRIVACY=private in .env while testing. Approve then publish.

how.all: python -m socialbot.cli approve <id> && python -m socialbot.cli publish <id> --targets youtube

setup_steps.title: (Optional) Automate it in the cloud
setup_steps.what: Follow 'deploy_github_actions' to run Oddjob on a schedule with no computer on.
setup_steps.verify: A manual run from the GitHub Actions tab succeeds.

steps: Go to https://aistudio.google.com/apikey
Click 'Create API key'
Copy the key
Paste it in .env after GEMINI_API_KEY=
gemini.free_note: Free tier is enough for testing and ~3 posts/day. For heavier use, attach billing in Google Cloud — same key, just higher limits.

steps: Make a free account at https://www.pexels.com/api/
Copy your API key
Paste it in .env after PEXELS_API_KEY=
Open https://console.cloud.google.com and create or pick a project
APIs & Services -> Enable APIs -> search 'YouTube Data API v3' -> Enable
OAuth consent screen -> choose External -> add your own email as a Test user
On the OAuth consent screen click 'Publish app' to move it from Testing to 'In production' (accept the unverified-app notice; this is REQUIRED so the token does not expire)
Credentials -> Create Credentials -> OAuth client ID -> Application type: Desktop app
Download the JSON file and save it as secrets/youtube_client_secret.json inside the Oddjob folder
Run: python -m socialbot.cli youtube-auth  (a browser opens; approve it)
youtube.important: You MUST publish the OAuth app to 'In production'. While it is in 'Testing' status Google expires the refresh token after 7 DAYS and the bot stops posting. In production the token is long-lived. Fix: OAuth consent screen -> Publish app (accept the unverified-app notice, fine for your own use), then re-run youtube-auth to get a fresh long-lived token.

steps: Optional. Works with no key (50 requests/day).
For more, register free at https://api.nasa.gov/ and the bot picks it up.
Create a Facebook Page
At https://developers.facebook.com create a Business app, add Graph API
Generate a Page access token with pages_manage_posts + pages_read_engagement, exchange it for a long-lived token
Put FACEBOOK_PAGE_ID and FACEBOOK_PAGE_TOKEN in .env

commands._prefix: Always run inside the project folder with the virtual environment active.

list_voices.does: Lists 200+ AI voices you can put in TTS_VOICES.

preview_trends.does: Shows what's trending in your niche without making a video (uses 1 API call).

make_video.does: Find topic -> script -> fact-check -> render to the review queue (does NOT post).

custom_topic.cmd: python -m socialbot.cli generate --topic "Your Title" --facts "the key facts" --keywords "word1,word2"
custom_topic.does: Make a video about YOUR topic instead of trending news.

auto_post.does: Fully automatic: generate + fact-check + post. Used by the cloud schedule.

promo.cmd: python -m socialbot.cli promo --title "My Song" --audio song.mp3 --image cover.jpg --link "https://..." --cta "Stream now" --publish
promo.does: Turn your OWN song/product/link into a post. See 'promo_mode'.

review_queue.cmd: python -m socialbot.cli list   |   show <id>   |   open <id>   |   approve <id>   |   reject <id>
review_queue.does: Browse, preview, and decide on queued videos.

costs.does: Show how much you've spent (free tier = $0).

dashboard.does: Open a web page to review/approve videos with buttons instead of commands.

promo_mode.what: Promote your own content with a clickable link. No trends, no fact-check.
promo_mode.audio: --audio yoursong.mp3 uses your track (trimmed to 60s with a fade-out). OR --say "text" makes an AI voiceover instead.
promo_mode.visuals: --video clip.mp4 or --image cover.jpg uses your media. Otherwise --keywords "a,b" pulls stock footage, or you get a gradient.
promo_mode.link: --link URL and --cta "label" add a clickable call-to-action to the description.

examples.song: python -m socialbot.cli promo --title "Midnight - out now" --audio midnight.mp3 --image cover.jpg --link "https://open.spotify.com/track/XXXX" --cta "Stream now" --hashtags "newmusic,indie" --publish
examples.product: python -m socialbot.cli promo --title "Meet Model X" --say "Launches today. 10-hour battery, waterproof." --video modelx.mp4 --link "https://shop.example.com" --cta "Shop now" --publish
examples.website: python -m socialbot.cli promo --title "We launched!" --say "Sign up free today." --keywords "startup,technology" --link "https://example.com" --cta "Visit"

config.where: Edit these in .env for local use, OR set them as GitHub Variables for the cloud schedule.
config.CONTENT_NICHE: Topics to cover. Be specific. e.g. 'electric vehicles, Tesla, EV charging'.
config.CONTENT_TONE: Narrator personality. e.g. 'calm analytical investor voice, no hype'.
config.CLIP_SECONDS: Video length. 15-30 is best for Shorts. Default 25.
config.TTS_VOICES: Comma-separated voices to rotate through. Run the voices command to list them.
config.YOUTUBE_PRIVACY: public, unlisted, or private. Use private while testing.
config.SPECULATIVE_KEYWORDS: Topics allowed to post even when unverifiable (e.g. ufo,alien). Others need a clean fact-check.
config.POSTS_PER_RUN: How many clips per scheduled run (cloud). Default 2.

tech_ai.CONTENT_NICHE: AI and emerging technology, space and astronomy, UFOs/UAPs
tech_ai.CONTENT_TONE: clear, punchy, plain-spoken explainer; neutral, no hype

business.CONTENT_TONE: confident brand voice, informative not salesy

finance.CONTENT_NICHE: stock market, crypto, personal finance, Fed news

fitness.CONTENT_NICHE: fitness research, nutrition science, workout trends
fitness.CONTENT_TONE: motivating but evidence-based, no miracle claims

gaming.CONTENT_NICHE: game releases, esports, gaming industry news

true_crime.CONTENT_NICHE: unsolved crimes, cold cases, forensic breakthroughs

deploy_github_actions.what: Runs Oddjob automatically on a schedule using GitHub's free servers. No computer needs to be on.
steps: Push the project to a PRIVATE GitHub repository.
In the repo: Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions.
Add SECRETS (encrypted): GEMINI_API_KEY, PEXELS_API_KEY (optional), and YOUTUBE_TOKEN (paste the full contents of secrets/youtube_token.json that youtube-auth created).
Add VARIABLES (plain config you can change anytime): CONTENT_NICHE, CONTENT_TONE, CLIP_SECONDS, TTS_VOICES, YOUTUBE_PRIVACY, POSTS_PER_RUN.
The schedule (.github/workflows/auto.yml) runs at 13:00, 18:00, 23:00 UTC. Edit the cron lines for your timezone.
Test it: Actions tab -> auto-post -> Run workflow.
deploy_github_actions.pause: To pause the cloud schedule, disable the workflow in the Actions tab.
deploy_github_actions.keep_private: Keep the repo PRIVATE — never commit your .env or secrets/ folder (they are git-ignored by default).

free_tier.per_video_calls: 3 (1 Flash for the script, 2 Flash-Lite for trends + fact-check). Promo mode with --audio uses fewer.
free_tier.free_ceiling: About 17-19 videos/day before the 20/day Gemini limit is reached.
free_tier.note: Check your own limits at https://aistudio.google.com/rate-limit . Google changes them occasionally.

costs.always_free: YouTube uploading, AI voiceover, Pexels footage, NASA footage.

troubleshooting.fix: You skipped step 5. Open .env and paste your key after GEMINI_API_KEY=.
ffmpeg isn't installed or not on your PATH. Reinstall it (what_you_need.software) and confirm 'ffmpeg -version' works.
The fact-checker held the topic (unverifiable or contradicted). Normal occasionally. Generating 2/run gives a buffer.

troubleshooting.symptom: Gemini calls fail after a few videos
troubleshooting.fix: You hit the free 20/day limit. Wait for the daily reset (midnight Pacific) or attach billing for higher limits.

Your OAuth app is still in 'Testing' status, where Google expires the token after 7 days. Go to Google Cloud Console -> OAuth consent screen -> Publish app (move to 'In production'), then re-run youtube-auth and update the YOUTUBE_TOKEN secret with the new token.
Make CONTENT_NICHE and your keywords more specific and concrete.

first_run_checklist: OAuth consent screen is published to 'In production' (so the token doesn't die after 7 days)
generate --count 1 produced a clip you watched
